reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
This chart shows the types of cookies sold by the local bakery.

[Image: Pie chart titled Cookies Sold, shaded and divided into various sizes; sugar about one-fourth, chocolate chip more than one-fourth, oatmeal more than one-half, and vanilla about one-eighth.]

Which type of cookie did the bakery sell the most of?
reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart titled "Cookies Sold" is divided into four unequal sectors:
- "sugar": light-gray shading, occupying the top-right quadrant from the 12 o'clock position to the 3 o'clock position (a right angle, exactly one-quarter of the circle).
- "chocolate chip": medium-gray shading, occupying the sector from the 3 o'clock position to approximately the 5 o'clock position.
- "oatmeal": white (unshaded), occupying the largest sector from approximately the 5 o'clock position counter-clockwise around the bottom and left to approximately the 10:30 position.
- "vanilla": white (unshaded), occupying the sector from approximately the 10:30 position to the 12 o'clock position.
Visually, oatmeal is the largest sector, sugar is the second largest, chocolate chip is third, and vanilla is the smallest.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Geometry Tiles
Instruction:

For this item, you have been given a piece of cardboard with 6 tiles like the ones shown below. Take the piece of cardboard, and punch out the 6 tiles.

If you do not have the piece of cardboard, raise your hand.

4 Triangle Tiles
[Image: Four triangle tiles]

2 Trapezoid Tiles
[Image: Two trapezoid tiles]

These tiles can be used to make new figures. One problem has been done for you

USE: 3 Triangle Tiles
MAKE: A trapezoid
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.
[Image: Example showing a trapezoid drawn on the grid]

Now try these problems.

C.

USE: 2 Trapezoid Tiles
MAKE: A 6-sided figure that is not the same shape as the one you made in Part B
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.

[Image: Triangular grid]

descriptors: Any of four figures (6-sided) that was not used in part B.
Repeats a correct figure already given in part B
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes four diagrams:
1. '4 Triangle Tiles': Four identical equilateral triangles of unit side length, arranged in a row pointing alternately up, down, up, and down.
2. '2 Trapezoid Tiles': Two identical isosceles trapezoids each composed of three equilateral triangle units (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit, legs 1 unit for the first one; and inverted with top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit for the second one).
3. Worked example grid: An isometric grid forming a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 3 units each and slanted sides of 2 units each, divided by dashed lines into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangles. In the top-right portion, a trapezoid made of 3 triangle units (top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) is outlined in bold solid lines.
4. Part C response grid: An identical empty parallelogram-shaped isometric grid with top and bottom edges of 3 units, slanted sides of 2 units, divided into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangle units by dashed lines.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Each figure represents a fraction.

[Image: Four figures labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4]

Which two figures represent the same fraction?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four rectangular figures labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4:
- Figure 1: A rectangle divided vertically into 4 equal strips; the 3 strips on the left are shaded gray, and the 1 strip on the right is unshaded white.
- Figure 2: A rectangle divided into a grid of 2 rows and 4 columns (8 equal parts); the 2 parts in the first column on the left are unshaded white, and the 6 parts in the other 3 columns are shaded gray.
- Figure 3: A rectangle divided vertically into 3 equal strips; the 2 strips on the left are shaded gray, and the 1 strip on the right is unshaded white.
- Figure 4: A rectangle divided into a grid of 2 rows and 2 columns (4 equal parts); the 2 parts in the left column are unshaded white, and the 2 parts in the right column are shaded gray.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
